newsitem.title: USA: U.S. names CIA Moscow spy suspect.
newsitem.headline: U.S. names CIA Moscow spy suspect.

text.p: The U.S. government said Monday it would charge Harold Nicholson, a veteran CIA officer, with conspiracy to commit espionage.

At a two-minute preliminary federal court hearing, U.S. Assistant Attorney Robert Chesnut, the prosecutor, gave no details of the charges. Other U.S. officials said Nicholson was accused of selling secrets to Moscow for at least two years.
Chesnut said death was the maximum penalty, in certain circumstances, for someone convicted on the charge.
Federal magistrate Thomas Rawles Jones of the District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia recessed the hearing until 2 p.m. (1900 GMT) because Nicholson did not have a lawyer with him.
Nicholson, white and bearded, wore a short-sleeved blue shirt and khaki pants.
U.S. officials said the Nicholson case appeared to have no link to Aldrich Ames, a 31-year CIA veteran arrested in 1994 after betraying some three dozen agents and perhaps hundreds of operations.
